This is a subtle and lively version of one of Shakespeare's greatest comedies, full of light, laughter and love.

Giving Shakespeare’s frothy bucolic romance a bold, visually arresting presentation and an all-male cast, director Daniel Evans’ ambitious production is unafraid to take risks. And despite significant technical issues on press night, the result is warm, earnest and unabashedly entertaining.

More than an hour passed before the actors returned to the stage, cheered on by an audience that was clearly anxious to see more of Jonathan Groff’s winningly vulnerable Rosalind. This was, remarkably enough, the American star’s Shakespearean debut.

cn.t: Critics praise this inventive all-male production's bold performances and fresh take on the classic, though both reviews were interrupted by technical difficulties that halted the show mid-performance.
